title: Goal Parser
description: A command string is built from `G`, `()` and `(al)`. Interpret it: `G` stays `G`, `()` becomes `o`, and `(al)` becomes `al`. Return the interpreted string.

title: Merge Strings Alternately
description: Weave two strings together by taking characters alternately, starting with `word1`. If one string is longer, append its remaining letters at the end.

examples.explanation: a p b q c r.
After a p b q, the rest "rs" is appended.

title: Halves Are Alike
description: Split an even-length string `s` into two equal halves. Return true if both halves contain the same number of vowels (a, e, i, o, u in either case).

title: Jewels and Stones
description: `jewels` lists the types of stones that are jewels, and `stones` is what you hold. Each character is one stone, and letters are case-sensitive. Return how many of your stones are jewels.

title: Count Odd Numbers in Range
description: Return how many odd numbers lie between `low` and `high`, both inclusive.

title: Sum of Unique Elements
description: Return the sum of the elements that appear exactly once in `nums`.

title: Sum of All Odd Length Subarrays
description: Return the sum of all subarrays of `arr` that have an odd length.

title: Decompress Run-Length List
description: `nums` holds pairs `[freq, val]` flattened (so `nums[2i]` is a frequency and `nums[2i+1]` the value). Expand each pair into `freq` copies of `val` and concatenate everything.

title: Steps to Reduce a Number to Zero
description: Each step: if the number is even divide it by 2, otherwise subtract 1. Return the number of steps to reach 0.

title: Subtract the Product and Sum of Digits
description: Return (product of the digits of `n`) minus (sum of the digits of `n`).

title: Palindrome Permutation
description: Return true if some rearrangement of the letters of `s` forms a palindrome.

examples.explanation: Too many letters with odd counts.

title: Maximum Number of Words in a Sentence
description: Each element of `sentences` is a sentence of words separated by single spaces. Return the largest word count among them.

examples.input: sentences = ["alice and bob love leetcode","i think so too","this is great thanks very much"]
sentences = ["please wait","continue to fight","continue to win"]

constraints: Lowercase words separated by single spaces

args: this is great thanks very much

title: Check If Array Is Sorted and Rotated
description: Return true if `nums` was originally sorted in non-decreasing order and then rotated by some number of positions (possibly zero).

examples.explanation: No rotation of a sorted array gives this.

title: Contiguous Array
description: Given a binary array `nums`, return the length of the longest contiguous subarray with an equal number of 0s and 1s.

title: Rotting Oranges
description: Grid cells: 0 empty, 1 fresh orange, 2 rotten orange. Every minute, each fresh orange adjacent (4 directions) to a rotten one becomes rotten. Return the minutes until no fresh orange remains, or -1 if some can never rot.

title: Course Schedule Feasibility
description: There are `numCourses` courses numbered 0..n-1. Each pair `[a, b]` in `prerequisites` means you must take `b` before `a`. Return true if it is possible to finish all courses.

title: Valid Sudoku Board
description: A 9×9 board uses 0 for an empty cell and 1–9 for filled cells. Return true if the filled cells obey the Sudoku rules: no repeated digit in any row, any column, or any of the nine 3×3 boxes. (The board need not be solvable.)

examples.explanation: No row, column or box repeats a digit.

examples.input: board = (a board with two 5s in the first row)

title: Generate Parentheses
description: Return every well-formed string of `n` pairs of parentheses, sorted in ascending (lexicographic) order.

title: Phone Letter Combinations
description: On a phone keypad 2=abc, 3=def, 4=ghi, 5=jkl, 6=mno, 7=pqrs, 8=tuv, 9=wxyz. Given a string of digits 2–9, return all possible letter strings sorted in ascending order.

title: Combination Sum
description: Given distinct positive integers `candidates` and a `target`, return every unique combination that sums to `target`. Each number may be reused unlimited times. Write each combination in ascending order and sort the list of combinations lexicographically.

title: Number of Provinces
description: `isConnected[i][j] = 1` means cities `i` and `j` are directly linked (links are symmetric). A province is a group of cities connected directly or indirectly. Return the number of provinces.

examples.explanation: Cities 0 and 1 form one province, city 2 another.

title: Meeting Rooms II
description: Given meeting time intervals `[start, end)`, return the minimum number of rooms required so that no two overlapping meetings share a room. A meeting ending at time t doesn't conflict with one starting at t.

title: Sort Characters By Frequency
description: Rearrange `s` so characters appear in decreasing order of frequency, with equal letters grouped together. If two characters share a frequency, put the one with the smaller ASCII value first.

examples.explanation: e appears twice; r and t once (r before t).

title: Valid Parenthesis String
description: `s` contains `(`, `)` and `*`. A `*` may act as `(`, `)` or an empty string. Return true if `s` can become a balanced parentheses string.

title: Car Pooling
description: A vehicle with `capacity` seats only drives forward. Each trip `[passengers, from, to]` boards at `from` and gets off at `to` (before anyone boards at that same point). Return true if every trip can be completed without ever exceeding capacity.

title: Maximum Points From Cards
description: Cards lie in a row with values `cardPoints`. In `k` steps you take one card per step from either end. Return the maximum total points.

title: Next Greater Element in a Circle
description: `nums` is circular: after the last element comes the first. For every element, return the first strictly greater value you meet moving forward around the circle, or -1 if none exists.

examples.explanation: The last 1 wraps around to find 2.
Each finds the next larger; 4 has none.

title: Remove K Digits
description: Given a number as a string `num`, remove exactly `k` digits so the remaining number is as small as possible. Return it without leading zeros (return "0" if nothing remains).

title: Permutations
description: Given distinct integers `nums`, return all their permutations, sorted in lexicographic order.

title: Binary Subarrays With Sum
description: Given a binary array `nums` and an integer `goal`, return the number of non-empty contiguous subarrays whose sum equals `goal`.

title: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix
description: In an n×n grid of 0 (open) and 1 (blocked), travel from the top-left to the bottom-right through open cells, moving in any of 8 directions. Return the number of cells on the shortest path, or -1 if none exists.

title: Distance to Nearest Zero
description: Given a binary matrix that contains at least one 0, return a matrix where each cell holds its Manhattan distance (4-directional steps) to the nearest 0.

examples.explanation: Only the centre is away from a zero.

title: Network Delay Time
description: A network has nodes 1..n and directed edges `times[i] = [u, v, w]` meaning a signal travels u→v in `w` time. A signal starts at node `k`. Return the time for all nodes to receive it, or -1 if some node never does.

title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
description: There are `n` cities and flights `[from, to, price]`. Find the cheapest price from `src` to `dst` using at most `k` stops (intermediate cities), or -1 if impossible.

title: Word Ladder Length
description: Transform `beginWord` into `endWord` by changing one letter at a time, where every intermediate word must be in `wordList` (the end word included). Return the number of words in the shortest sequence (counting both ends), or 0 if impossible.

examples.explanation: hit → hot → dot → dog → cog: 5 words.
The end word isn't in the list.

constraints: All words have the same length

title: Total N-Queens
description: Place `n` queens on an `n × n` chessboard so no two attack each other (same row, column or diagonal). Return the number of distinct solutions.

title: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
description: From any cell you may move up, down, left or right (no diagonals, no leaving the grid) to a cell with a strictly larger value. Return the length of the longest such path.

title: Dungeon Game
description: A knight starts at the top-left of a grid and must reach the bottom-right, moving only right or down. Each cell changes his health by `dungeon[i][j]` (negative = damage). His health must stay at least 1 at all times, including after the last cell. Return the minimum starting health required.

examples.explanation: Going right, right, down, down needs 7 health.
Health can never drop below 1, so 1.

title: Palindrome Partitioning Minimum Cuts
description: Cut the string `s` into pieces so every piece is a palindrome. Return the minimum number of cuts needed.

title: Interleaving String
description: Return true if `s3` can be formed by interleaving all characters of `s1` and `s2` while preserving the relative order of characters within each of them.
